final_candidates.decision_summary: Proline at L65 is exceptionally incompatible with the experimental backbone and sequence model and is absent among covered homologs. Its helix-breaking character makes strong fold destabilization likely.

Replacing conserved F60 with a charged aspartate is strongly sequence-implausible, evolutionarily unsupported, and poorly compatible with the backbone. These independent signals support substantial destabilization.

Y18D introduces a charged residue at a conserved aromatic position and has very low sequence and structural compatibility. Full MSA coverage with no observed mutant residue further supports intolerance.

stop_reason.detail: The leading three candidates are supported by concordant evidence, while the remaining tool call is unlikely to change their ranking.

history.rationale: Replaces a bulky aromatic residue with a charged acidic residue, likely disrupting hydrophobic packing in this compact protein.

The substitution is evolutionarily absent and sequence-implausible, but ProteinMPNN indicates only modest structural incompatibility. It remains plausible as a disruptive aromatic-to-charge mutation but falls below candidates with stronger structural evidence.
Complete evolutionary absence and near-zero sequence plausibility support intolerance, but moderate backbone compatibility makes severe folding disruption less certain.
Introduces a negative charge adjacent to W17 in an aromatic-rich segment, potentially destabilizing the local fold.

Y18D has strong backbone incompatibility and very low sequence plausibility, consistent with disruption by introducing charge at an aromatic position. Full MSA coverage with no observed aspartate strengthens the deleteriousness prior.
The substitution is absent from well-covered homologs, highly implausible to the sequence model, and poorly compatible with the fixed backbone. It remains a strong predicted folding disruptor.
Proline can disrupt regular backbone geometry; introducing it within the hydrophobic central region may strongly impair folding.

Although proline is absent from homologs and sequence-implausible, ProteinMPNN slightly favors it on the experimental backbone. That direct structural-context evidence makes severe fold disruption less likely than for the leading candidates.

rejection.reason: Although proline is absent from homologs and sequence-implausible, ProteinMPNN slightly favors it on the experimental backbone. That direct structural-context evidence makes severe fold disruption less likely than for the leading candidates.

history.rationale: Substitution of an aromatic residue by aspartate may remove core packing and introduce an unfavorable buried charge.
Despite evolutionary and sequence-model implausibility, ProteinMPNN slightly favors aspartate on the fixed backbone at position 34. This argues against Y34D being a reliable folding destabilizer.

rejection.reason: Despite evolutionary and sequence-model implausibility, ProteinMPNN slightly favors aspartate on the fixed backbone at position 34. This argues against Y34D being a reliable folding destabilizer.

history.rationale: Replacing phenylalanine with aspartate combines loss of aromatic packing with introduction of charge, making it a strong destabilization candidate.

Backbone and language-model evidence suggest strong incompatibility, but aspartate occurs at this position in about 19% of aligned homologs. That natural tolerance substantially reduces confidence that F40D will reliably unfold PsaE.

Very low sequence plausibility and low structural compatibility favor disruption, although measurable evolutionary occurrence weakens the case. It remains below the three candidates with cleaner intolerance signals.
This radical aromatic-to-acidic substitution may disrupt packing near the glycine-rich region and compromise fold stability.

ProteinMPNN finds F48D relatively compatible with the experimental backbone, and it is the most sequence-plausible candidate in the pool. The low-coverage evolutionary result is insufficient to rescue it as a strong folding-disruption candidate.

rejection.reason: ProteinMPNN finds F48D relatively compatible with the experimental backbone, and it is the most sequence-plausible candidate in the pool. The low-coverage evolutionary result is insufficient to rescue it as a strong folding-disruption candidate.

history.rationale: Replacing the sole aromatic residue in the C-terminal segment with an acidic residue could destabilize a hydrophobic structural anchor.

Replacing F60 with a charged aspartate is strongly incompatible with the experimental backbone and is absent among well-covered homologs. These signals favor substantial structural disruption, although none directly measures folding stability.
Replacing a conserved aromatic residue with an acidic residue is strongly sequence-implausible and poorly compatible with the experimental backbone. These complementary signals favor destabilization.
A proline near the C terminus may break local secondary structure and interfere with formation of the native fold.

This is the strongest fixed-backbone incompatibility in the pool, and proline at L65 may disrupt the structured C-terminal segment. Its extreme sequence implausibility and absence from covered homologs provide additional, indirect support.
Extremely low backbone compatibility and sequence plausibility support strong disruption by a helix-breaking proline. Its absence among covered homologs adds indirect evidence of intolerance.
This hydrophobic-to-charged substitution could destabilize C-terminal packing, although its proximity to the terminus may reduce the effect.
V67D is non-natural in the available partial alignment and sequence-implausible, but its moderate backbone compatibility and near-terminal location weaken the folding-disruption hypothesis.

The substitution is sequence-implausible and unobserved among available homologs, but structural compatibility is only moderately unfavorable and evolutionary coverage is limited. Its terminal location also reduces confidence in global fold disruption.
